 The Los Angeles Lakers face local rivals without a major star.
 The Lakers will play an away game against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, California on the 29th (Korea Standard Time). The previous day, he played a home game against the Portland Trail Blazers and had a back-to-back without moving.
 Luka Doncic (back strain) and Jaire Williams (left foot inflammation and pain) will be absent from the Lakers on this day. Doncic scored 41 points while running 36 minutes and 45 seconds the previous day, while Williams ran 28 minutes and 41 seconds and scored 11 points.
 사진 확대 Luka Doncic will miss the away game against the Clippers. Photo = AP= Courtesy of Yonhap News Coach JJ Redic said in an interview before the game, "Both players said they felt sick after sleeping and waking up. Luca has tension, Williams has pain. As you know, I have a tight schedule recently and I don't have a lot of time off, so I'm going to go carefully," he said about the absence of the two players.
 Regarding Doncic, when asked if he would be able to play in the away game against the Golden State Warriors in two days, he briefly replied, "I hope so."
 In the absence of Doncic, Austin Reeves' weight is bound to increase. Clippers coach Tyronn Lue expressed caution about Reeves, calling him a "difficult player." "I had a chance to see him in the playoffs last season. I was impressed by the way the game was run and the way he made important shots and made plays at the destination. He is a versatile player. He can shoot 3-pointers, score points in the paint zone, throw pull-up jumpers, and pass skills. Breakthrough is possible in both directions. He's really good at getting fouls, too. He is an outstanding player in every way. We must never let our guard down," he said.
 사진 확대 Reeves' role became more important in the absence of Doncic. Photo = Getty Images via AFP = Courtesy of Yonhap News Ledick said, "If a player like Luca falls out, it is natural that the opportunity and possession go to another player. However, I don't want players to force them to play a role other than who they are. We need to continue to maintain a systematic appearance and create an environment where players can show their strengths, such as directing operations, making more use of set plays, or making changes to the lineup, he said of how to deal with Doncic's gap.
 Ledick, who allowed the Portland Trail Blazers their first loss of the season the day before as the defense faltered, said, "We are a newly formed team and some players are still unfamiliar with our team's tactics and terms. I don't think we've been able to show the way we intended to defend the last two games or the form of defense we're asking our players to do. We have a lot of capable defenders on our team. I'm sure that over time, the defense will also get back on track. It is necessary to be disciplined in defensive position movement, close-out, and defense that determines the direction of the opponent. "I'll get better gradually," he said, expressing confidence that he will show better performance in defense.
 He compared the early part of the season to "the process of drawing a map" and said, "It's a step to try various things and figure out what color our team has. Especially if it's a team with a lot of new players, it's necessary to get to know what type of players they are. Even if you've been watching players and observing the game for a long time, you have to figure out what role they should play within the team and how to put them in a position to succeed. That part is still a process for all of our players to refine," he added.
 사진 확대 Kessler is showing his presence under the Lakers goal. Photo = AP= Courtesy of Yonhap News The two teams met once on the 24th. At the time, the Lakers won 125-117. The Clippers were rocked with 26 turnovers for the entire team.
 Lou said, "We've been in good shape. With the right intention, he has been running the game at a fast tempo by sharing the ball. But you have to pay more attention to keeping the ball. Twenty-six turnovers in two consecutive games is too much. We are a team that cannot afford to make mistakes. Players are well aware of this. "I know that sometimes we are asking the players to play a role beyond their capabilities, but we still have to faithfully do the basics and keep the ball well," he said, calling for the players to make their best efforts.
 Regarding the countermeasure against center Walker Kessler, who allowed six block shots in the previous match, he said, "We have to keep our own color. We need to continue our original play of actively targeting the paint zone. When Kessler is guarding the paint zone, he said, "We have to be smart to respond to the situation, such as giving a pass to a colleague or taking it out to the outside."
 [Inglewood (USA) = KIM JAE HO, MK Sports Correspondent]
